item.title: EU nations back military space project worth up to $27 billion, propose shared tracking data
item.description: JOHANNESBURG — European governments are preparing to invest up to 24 billion euros ($27 billion) in SPACE, a joint military space project spanning satellite communications, surveillance and missile warning. The initiative is part of a broader EU effort to expand its defense capabilities in orbit.

item.description: SpaceX launched a new crew to the International Space Station on Oct. 1 on a mission delayed by repairs to the Crew Dragon spacecraft.

item.title: Too close for comfort: undisclosed U.S. space weapons and the risk of miscalculation
item.description: When a spacecraft closes in on another satellite, the operator tracking its trajectory on the other side now also has to consider whether that spacecraft is a weapon. On Sept. 14, 2026, Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink revealed that the United States has “on-orbit space control weapons” to defend United States forces. Then Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess confirmed that Space Force personnel operate weapons in orbit . The world now knows that American weapons are in orbit, but since officials left their number, capabilities and locations undisclosed, there is no reliable public way to tell them apart from other spacecraft. For other operators, that silence adds to the dual-use dilemma, since an American spacecraft that appears to be inspecting or servicing a satellite may now turn out to be one of those weapons.

item.title: Foundational emerges from stealth to commercialize satellite laser ranging
item.description: British startup Foundational emerged from stealth Oct. 1 with nearly $11 million in funding to upgrade and commercialize Satellite Laser Ranging, a decades-old technology for pinpointing satellites in orbit used mainly by scientific and government groups.
